Forum Overview

About the Forum

The South Asia Drone Forum brought together regional stakeholders to discuss the future of unmanned aviation across South Asia — policy, innovation, and cross-border collaboration.

  • calendar_today 9–11 April 2025, Kathmandu
  • groups Co-organized by Government of Nepal, World Bank & KWPF
  • public Regional platform bringing together South Asia's drone ecosystem
  • flight UDAAN represented Nepal's unmanned aviation community on the regional stage

About the South Asia Drone Forum 2025

The forum ran from 9 to 11 April 2025 in Kathmandu. It was hosted by the Government of Nepal through the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, in partnership with the World Bank and with funding from the Korea–World Bank Partnership Facility (KWPF).

The World Bank describes it as the first South Asia Drone Forum and a milestone of its Drone Ecosystem Acceleration Program (DEAP), launched in 2023 to support the safe and inclusive use of drones in Nepal.

Who took part

Civil aviation authorities from seven South Asian countries attended, along with about 45 regional experts who shared how drone policy and drone use work in their countries. Delegates also came from Africa, Europe and the United States.

The programme included live demonstrations of drones built in the region, among them a 1 kg food delivery flown in a designated drone corridor in Kathmandu.

What was discussed

  • How drones are used for disaster response, healthcare delivery, agriculture and environmental monitoring
  • Drone policy and regulation, including how complicated it is to register a drone in Nepal when permission is needed from more than one agency
  • Regional policy alignment, testing infrastructure and building local skills

Why it matters for UDAAN

These are the same issues UDAAN works on. In the same week as the forum, UDAAN wrote to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation about a roughly 400-fold increase in drone registration fees. UDAAN has since supervised professional drone training and signed an MoU with NDRRMA on disaster response.
